Modern neuroscience of personality and decision-making begins.

ticks.name: Elevator safety brake (Otis)
ticks.constraint: building height limited by stair-climbing practicality
ticks.detail: The skyscraper, the vertical city, and urban density all become possible.

links.label: PBS: Who Made America? — Elisha Otis

ticks.because: The Rochdale Principles (1844) had built the cooperative-movement template; the Chicago Board of Trade (1848) had introduced commodity futures; the California Gold Rush (1848) and refrigerated boxcar (1851) had each scaled commerce in unprecedented ways. Otis's safety brake — preventing free-fall when the rope breaks — is the unlock for vertical density. Skyscrapers, mass urbanism, and the modern city skyline depend on people willing to ride.

ticks.name: Boolean algebra (Boole)
ticks.constraint: logic as verbal and informal
ticks.detail: Every computer processor is Boolean algebra made physical.

links.label: Project Gutenberg: Boole, Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854)

ticks.because: Kierkegaard's existential anxiety (1843), the Communist Manifesto (1848), and Stirner's egoism (1844) had each treated philosophical fundamentals as open to systematic critique. Boole's Laws of Thought is the formal counterpart — logic reduced to algebra, with binary values and operations matching set-theoretic union and intersection. The mathematical foundation of every digital circuit a century later.

ticks.name: Synthetic dye (Perkin's mauveine)
ticks.constraint: color requiring rare organic sources
ticks.detail: The chemical industry as a separate industry begins here.

links.label: Wiley: Sir William Henry Perkin — life, work, legacy

ticks.because: The Chicago Board of Trade (1848), the Otis safety brake (1852), and the Limited Liability Act (1855) had each restructured economic risk so that capital could fund specialized ventures. Perkin's accidental synthesis of mauveine — looking for synthetic quinine, finding a brilliant purple dye — is the first commercial product of synthetic organic chemistry. The chemical industry's modern shape begins here.

ticks.name: On the Origin of Species (Darwin)
ticks.constraint: species as fixed and divinely created
ticks.detail: The most destabilizing scientific idea in history.

links.label: Darwin Online — On the Origin of Species (1859, 1st ed.)
American Museum of Natural History — Darwin

ticks.because: Schleiden-Schwann cell theory (1839) had unified biology under cellular construction. Mendel's inheritance rules (1856) — though unread — had quantified discrete heritable variation. The Darwin-Wallace joint Linnean Society paper (1858) made the public claim. On the Origin of Species is Darwin's book-length argument — variation plus selection plus deep time produces adaptation, no designer required. The most destabilizing scientific idea in history.

ticks.name: Broca's area (language localization)
ticks.constraint: brain as homogeneous and non-localized
ticks.detail: The brain has specific regions for specific functions. Neuroimaging begins with this discovery.

links.label: Berker et al. — Translation of Broca's 1865 Report (JAMA Neurology)

ticks.because: Phineas Gage's frontal lobe case (1848), John Snow's cholera epidemiology (1854), and Mendel's inheritance rules (1856) demonstrated that careful systematic observation could localize causes. Broca's identification of the brain region whose damage produces aphasia — Broca's area, in the left frontal lobe — establishes that the brain has specific regions for specific functions. Modern neuroimaging and cognitive neuroscience inherit this principle.

ticks.name: Germ theory (Pasteur/Koch)
ticks.constraint: disease as caused by miasma or internal imbalance
ticks.detail: Life expectancy doubled in the century after this tick.

links.label: John Waller — The Discovery of the Germ

ticks.because: John Snow's cholera-and-epidemiology work (1854) and Broca's localization of language in the brain (1861) demonstrated that systematic empirical investigation could identify specific causes of complex problems. Pasteur and Koch's parallel work in the 1860s — anthrax bacillus, Koch's postulates, the rabies vaccine — establishes that specific microbes cause specific diseases. Life expectancy doubles in the century after this tick.

ticks.name: Manet / Salon des Refusés
ticks.constraint: painting as requiring idealized or historically justified subjects
ticks.detail: Impressionism, modernism, and the avant-garde all begin here.
ticks.because: Roget's Thesaurus (1852) had organized vocabulary by concept. Photography's liberation of painting (1839, expanded 1863) freed artists from documentary obligation. Melville's Moby-Dick (1851) demonstrated that prose could absorb encyclopedic knowledge while sustaining literary ambition. Manet's Salon des Refusés exhibition is the visual-art parallel — works rejected by the academic Salon shown together, declaring an alternative aesthetic. Impressionism, modernism, and the avant-garde all begin here.

ticks.name: Geneva Convention
ticks.constraint: war as having no rules for treatment of the wounded
ticks.detail: The tick that war itself has legal constraints binding on all parties.
ticks.because: The Lieber Code (1863) and the Emancipation Proclamation (1863) bracket a year when the US Civil War was forcing the codification of the laws of war and the rights of persons in wartime. Henry Dunant, who had witnessed Solferino, organized the conference that produced the First Geneva Convention — neutral medical personnel, treatment of wounded combatants, the red cross emblem — and gave international humanitarian law its founding treaty.

ticks.name: Antiseptic surgery (Lister)
ticks.constraint: surgical infection as inevitable and mysterious
ticks.detail: Post-surgical mortality dropped from ~50% to ~15% almost immediately.

links.label: Lister — On the Antiseptic Principle in the Practice of Surgery (1867)
Fitzharris — The Butchering Art (biography of Lister)

ticks.because: Broca's area (1861) had localized language in specific brain tissue. Pasteur and Koch's germ theory (1861) had identified microbes as disease agents. Lister's application of carbolic acid to wounds, instruments, and the operating theater is the practical synthesis. Post-surgical mortality drops from about fifty percent to fifteen almost immediately; surgical infection becomes a managed problem.

ticks.name: Periodic table (Mendeleev)
ticks.constraint: elements as unrelated individuals
ticks.detail: Chemistry became a predictive science.
ticks.because: Kirchhoff-Bunsen spectroscopy (1859) gave chemistry a way to identify elements remotely. Maxwell's equations (1865) had unified electromagnetism. Maxwell's demon thought experiment (1867) had connected information and thermodynamics. Mendeleev's periodic table is the ordering principle — atomic weight and chemical behavior arranged so the gaps in the table predict missing elements before they're found. Chemistry becomes systematically predictive.

ticks.name: Set theory (Cantor)
ticks.constraint: infinity as a single undifferentiated concept
ticks.detail: Some infinities are larger than others. Foundation of all mathematics.

links.label: Stony Brook — Cantor's set theory paper (translation)

ticks.because: Boolean algebra (Boole, 1854) had reduced logic to algebraic operations. Mill's On the Subjection of Women (1869) showed that fundamental categories — gender, person, citizen — were open to systematic challenge. Cantor's set theory takes the algebraization to its logical limit — collections themselves become objects, and infinity becomes a measurable hierarchy. Modern mathematics's foundations begin here.

ticks.name: Telephone (Bell)
ticks.constraint: voice communication requiring physical proximity
ticks.detail: Restructured social space as completely as roads restructured physical space.

links.label: Library of Congress: Who invented the telephone?
University of Virginia (IATH): Bell's first patent (No. 174,465)

ticks.because: Marx's Das Kapital (1867), the marginal revolution (1871), the Trade Union Act (1871), and the typewriter (1874) bracket a period when industrial society was being analyzed and reorganized at the same time. Bell's telephone applied the same forces to communication: voice across wires, instant, two-way — and within a decade, the telephone exchange would make any subscriber reachable by any other, restructuring social space as completely as roads had restructured physical space.

ticks.name: Phonograph (Edison)
ticks.constraint: music as existing only in the moment of performance
ticks.detail: The entire recorded music industry, radio, and streaming descend from this tick.

links.label: Library of Congress: History of the Cylinder Phonograph

ticks.because: Bell's first telephone call (1876) had transmitted voice through wires. Braille (1837) had earlier shown that signal-encoding could be deliberately engineered. Photography's liberation of painting (1863) demonstrated that mechanical reproduction reorders art. Edison's phonograph applies all three insights to sound — captured, repeatable, transferable. The recorded music industry, radio, and streaming all descend from this device.

ticks.name: Electric light (Edison's grid system)
ticks.constraint: productive activity limited to daylight hours
ticks.detail: Electrification is the substrate for virtually all that follows.

links.label: U.S. Department of Energy — History of the Light Bulb

ticks.because: The marginal revolution (1871) had reframed economic value as flowing from utility at the margin, and Bell's telephone (1876) plus the early telephone exchange (1878) showed that distributing a service to households via wires was a workable business model. Edison applied the same model to light — generation, distribution, metered consumption — and made productive activity unbound from daylight hours.

ticks.name: Rabies vaccine (Pasteur / first viral vaccine)
ticks.constraint: viral disease as having no vaccine option
ticks.detail: Attenuated virus can train immunity without causing disease. All modern vaccines follow this logic.

links.label: Rappuoli — 1885, the first rabies vaccination in humans (PNAS)
PMC — 1885, the first rabies vaccination in humans
CDC — Pasteur and the Modern Era of Immunization

ticks.because: Lister's antiseptic surgery (1865) and his carbolic acid technique (1867) had demonstrated that microbial reasoning could transform medical practice. Miescher's discovery of DNA (1869) extended the molecular biology frontier. Pasteur's attenuated rabies virus, given to Joseph Meister in 1885, is the first viral vaccine — and the proof that whole pathogens can be deliberately weakened to train immunity. Every modern vaccine descends from this principle.

ticks.name: Eiffel Tower / wrought-iron architecture
ticks.constraint: masonry height limits
ticks.detail: Eiffel Tower (1889) used 7,300 tonnes of wrought puddle iron — not steel — to reach 300m, the tallest structure of its era.

links.label: Eiffel Tower Official: What is the Eiffel Tower made of? (puddle iron)

ticks.because: The International Phonetic Alphabet (1888) and the International Postal Union (1874) demonstrated that engineering of communicative systems could scale globally. Monet's Impression, Sunrise (1872) had made perception itself art's subject. The Eiffel Tower's wrought-iron exoskeleton — 7,300 tonnes of puddled iron, completed for the 1889 Paris Exposition — extends the engineering ambition to monumental architecture. Industrial design as public spectacle is born.

ticks.name: Principles of Psychology (William James)
ticks.constraint: mind as unitary and fully conscious
ticks.detail: Psychology split from philosophy. Foundation for pragmatism, functionalism, and cognitive psychology.

links.label: William James — The Principles of Psychology (Classics in History of Psychology, York U)
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — William James

ticks.because: Wundt's Leipzig laboratory (1879) had treated psychology as a measurable science of conscious elements. James's 1890 Principles of Psychology took the field in the opposite direction — treating consciousness as a continuous flowing stream, not a sum of atoms, and treating habit, emotion, and self as central. Psychology split definitively from philosophy. Pragmatism, functionalism, and most twentieth-century cognitive psychology trace back to this two-volume textbook.

ticks.name: Cinema (Lumière brothers)
ticks.constraint: storytelling requiring imagination to animate
ticks.detail: A century of film, propaganda, and mass entertainment follows.

links.label: National Geographic — How the Lumière brothers invented the movies

ticks.because: Edison's phonograph (1877) had proved that an analog signal could be captured and replayed. The Eiffel Tower (1889) had shown industrial spectacle as a commercial product. Joseph Swan's incandescent bulb (1881) provided the lighting for indoor projection. The Cinématographe is the synthesis — capture, projection, and a commercial venue. Cinema is born as a public spectacle.

ticks.name: X-ray (Röntgen)
ticks.constraint: the body as opaque to inspection
ticks.detail: Surgeons could plan operations without opening the patient.

links.label: Internet Archive: Röntgen, On a New Kind of Rays (Science 1896)
Bloomsbury Primary Source: Röntgen, The X-Rays (1895)

ticks.because: Lister's antiseptic technique (1867) and Pasteur's rabies vaccine (1885) demonstrated the era's accelerating biomedical sophistication. Fitz's surgical treatment of appendicitis (1886) showed what surgeons could do without internal vision. Röntgen's accidental discovery of X-rays in November 1895 changes everything — surgeons can plan operations without opening the patient, fractures can be precisely diagnosed, foreign objects located. Modern radiology begins immediately.

ticks.name: Radio waves (Marconi)
ticks.constraint: long-distance communication requiring physical wire
ticks.detail: Mass broadcasting — and mass persuasion — was born.

links.label: Oxford Museum of the History of Science: Marconi Collection
Marconi Heritage: Marconi and the invention of wireless

ticks.because: Edison's electric grid (1879) showed that long-distance distribution of energy was a workable business model, and Hertz's earlier detection of electromagnetic waves provided the physics. Marconi's transmitter and receiver collapsed wired distance for signals — first across rooms, then across oceans — and made wireless point-to-point communication a commercial reality.

ticks.name: Interpretation of Dreams (Freud)
ticks.constraint: behavior as fully explicable by conscious intention
ticks.detail: The unconscious as causally active. Psychotherapy and 'processing' emotions begin here.

links.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Sigmund Freud

ticks.because: Charcot's hypnosis demonstrations (1880s) had shown that the conscious mind doesn't have full access to its own causes. Freud's Interpretation of Dreams (1899) argued the unconscious was causally active in waking life as well — desires, fears, memories shaping action without the actor's awareness. Psychoanalysis as therapy followed. The subsequent century of personality psychology, psychotherapy, and pop self-help — 'processing' emotions, 'working through' issues — all assume Freud's unconscious is real.

ticks.name: Planck's quantum hypothesis
ticks.constraint: energy as continuously variable
ticks.detail: Nature is granular at the smallest scale. Quantum mechanics, semiconductors, lasers, and MRI all begin here.
ticks.because: Thomson's discovery of the electron (1897) and the Curies' isolation of polonium and radium (1898) had each pushed late-nineteenth-century physics into the subatomic realm. Planck's hypothesis — that radiation is emitted in discrete energy packets, E = hν — solves the black-body radiation problem and inadvertently births quantum mechanics. Nature is granular at the smallest scale; semiconductors, lasers, and the atomic age all stand on Planck's constant.

ticks.name: Blood typing (Landsteiner)
ticks.constraint: blood transfusion as fatally unpredictable
ticks.detail: ABO blood typing made transfusions safe. Trauma surgery and organ transplantation depend on this tick.
ticks.because: X-ray clinical use (1895) and Kraepelin's psychiatric classification (1899) demonstrated that medicine was acquiring systematic diagnostic categories. The rediscovery of Mendel (1900) provided the genetic frame. Landsteiner's identification of ABO blood groups explains why most transfusions had been killing patients — recipient and donor must be matched. Trauma surgery and eventually organ transplantation become routine on the back of this finding.

ticks.name: Powered flight (Wright brothers)
ticks.constraint: human movement limited to land and sea
ticks.detail: The world went from weeks-by-ship to hours-by-plane in one human lifetime.

links.label: Library of Congress — Wright Brothers Papers

ticks.because: Real-time telegraph command (1862) had collapsed strategic distance, and the Maxim gun (1884) had collapsed tactical distance. The physics that mattered for flight was simultaneously coming together — Michelson-Morley (1887) and the discovery of the electron (1897) signaled that nineteenth-century physics knew its limits — and the Wrights, working in a bicycle shop, used controlled wind-tunnel data and three-axis control to fly a heavier-than-air machine for twelve seconds.

ticks.name: Photoelectric effect / photons (Einstein)
ticks.constraint: light as purely wave-like
ticks.detail: Wave-particle duality. Quantum field theory and the conceptual crisis of quantum mechanics begin here.

links.label: AIP History — Einstein on the Photoelectric Effect (Cassidy)
Library of Congress — Einstein's 1905 Annus Mirabilis Papers

ticks.because: Planck's quantum hypothesis (1900) had just admitted granularity into nature at the smallest scale, and Thomson's electron (1897) plus the Curies' radium work (1898) showed that classical electromagnetism alone could not explain atomic-scale phenomena. Einstein's photoelectric paper turned Planck's accounting trick into physics: light is itself granular — photons — and wave-particle duality is real, not bookkeeping.

ticks.name: Special relativity (Einstein)
ticks.constraint: time and space as absolute and universal
ticks.detail: E=mc² means matter is frozen energy. Atomic energy, nuclear weapons, and MRI machines are direct applications.

links.label: Einstein — On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies (1905) — original paper
Walter Isaacson — Einstein: His Life and Universe

ticks.because: Planck's quantum hypothesis (1900) had introduced granularity into nature, and the photoelectric effect paper (1905) confirmed that light itself was discrete. Special relativity completed the same year's revolution from the opposite direction: Maxwell's equations are right, the speed of light is invariant, and time and space must therefore reorder themselves around any observer to keep that invariance true.

ticks.name: Cajal / neuron doctrine
ticks.constraint: nervous system as a continuous network
ticks.detail: The nervous system consists of discrete neurons communicating across synapses. Every psychoactive drug depends on understanding this.

links.label: Nobel Prize — Santiago Ramón y Cajal 1906
NCBI PMC — Santiago Ramón y Cajal and the neuron doctrine

ticks.because: Kraepelin's first psychiatric classification (1899) gave psychiatry its first systematic taxonomy. ABO blood typing (1901) demonstrated that human biological individuality had molecular markers. Cajal's silver-stain microscopy of nervous tissue resolves the longstanding question of brain structure — the nervous system is built of discrete neurons separated by gaps (later named synapses), not a continuous reticulum. Modern neuroscience begins.

ticks.name: Cubism (Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon)
ticks.constraint: painting as representing a single viewpoint
ticks.detail: The 20th century's visual language is cubism's consequence.

links.label: MoMA Gallery 502 — Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon

ticks.because: The Lumière screening (1895) had introduced motion-picture realism as a baseline for visual culture. The Great Train Robbery (1903) systematized cinematic narrative. Fauvism (1905) had demonstrated that color could be subjective and expressive rather than descriptive. Les Demoiselles d'Avignon takes the next step — pictorial space itself fractures, bodies become geometric, multiple viewpoints coexist in one frame. The visual language of the twentieth century begins.

ticks.name: Haber-Bosch nitrogen fixation
ticks.constraint: nitrogen fertilizer requiring biological sources
ticks.detail: Without Haber-Bosch, Earth could support ~3.5B people. We have 8B.

links.label: The Alchemy of Air — Thomas Hager

ticks.because: Refrigeration (1870), pasteurization of milk (1900), the rediscovery of Mendel (1900), and ABO blood typing (1900) bracket a moment when food, biology, and medicine were all being industrialized. The Haber-Bosch process (1909-1913) — fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia under high pressure and temperature — replaced biological nitrogen sources with industrial fertilizer, and now feeds approximately half the global population through synthesized nitrogen.

ticks.name: Continental drift hypothesis (Wegener)
ticks.constraint: the positions of continents as permanent and fixed
ticks.detail: Ridiculed for 40 years. The mechanism came later. The tick was the hypothesis.

links.label: USGS — Alfred Wegener and continental drift

ticks.because: Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom (1911) and Kamerlingh Onnes's discovery of superconductivity (1911) demonstrated that early-twentieth-century physics was rapidly revealing nature's deep structure. Wegener's continental drift hypothesis — that continents were once joined and have moved apart — is rejected for forty years for lack of mechanism. Plate tectonics in the 1960s provides the mechanism; the hypothesis is vindicated.

ticks.name: Bohr's atomic model
ticks.constraint: electrons as free to orbit at any radius
ticks.detail: Explained atomic spectra quantitatively for the first time.

links.label: Niels Bohr Institute — Bohr's atomic model
Bohr — On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules (Phil. Mag. 1913)

ticks.because: Wegener's continental drift hypothesis (1912), von Laue's X-ray crystallography (1912), and Hess's discovery of cosmic rays (1912) had each pushed early-twentieth-century physical science into radical new territory. Bohr's atomic model — electrons in discrete orbits emitting fixed-frequency photons when transitioning — explains atomic spectra quantitatively for the first time. Quantum mechanics's path forward becomes navigable.

ticks.name: Income tax (US 16th Amendment)
ticks.constraint: government revenue limited to tariffs and excise
ticks.detail: State capacity at scale is a tax story.
ticks.because: Husserl's phenomenology (1900) and Weber's Protestant Ethic (1905) demonstrated that early-twentieth-century social and philosophical thought was systematizing. The Geneva Convention (1864) had earlier shown that states could codify constraints on themselves. The 16th Amendment's authorization of federal income tax in 1913 enables state capacity at scale — modern Western governments, with their administrative depth and welfare programs, all run on the income-tax foundation.

ticks.name: US Federal Reserve established
ticks.constraint: US banking panics as unmanageable
ticks.detail: The institutional lender of last resort for the modern economy.

links.label: Federal Reserve: Centennial — About the Fed

ticks.because: US banking panics in the late nineteenth century (1873, 1893, 1907) had each required private rescue (J.P. Morgan personally backstopped 1907). The Aldrich-Vreeland Act (1908) was a stopgap; the Federal Reserve Act (December 1913) created an actual central bank: twelve regional reserve banks coordinated by a Washington board, lender of last resort to commercial banks, currency-issuing authority. The Great Depression (1929-39) tested the design and found it inadequate; the modern Fed evolved through the 1930s reforms. The institutional substrate of US monetary policy is now Fed-shaped.

ticks.name: Assembly line (Ford)
ticks.constraint: skill as the bottleneck of production
ticks.detail: Mass manufacturing. Consumer economy follows.

links.label: Ford Media: 100th Anniversary of the Moving Assembly Line
Ford Corporate: The Moving Assembly Line and the Five-Dollar Workday
Ford Motor History: The Assembly Line

ticks.because: Marconi's radio waves (1896) and Moody's first bond ratings (1909) bracket a period when both communication and capital allocation were being industrialized. Ford's moving assembly line at Highland Park — workers stationary, work moving past them — cut Model T production time from 12 hours to 90 minutes, dropped the unit cost dramatically, and made the automobile a mass-market consumer good rather than an artisan-built luxury.

ticks.name: Saussure's Course in General Linguistics
ticks.constraint: language as a collection of words with meanings
ticks.detail: Language is a system of differences. Structuralism and post-structuralism begin here.

links.label: Saussure — Course in General Linguistics (Internet Archive, Baskin trans.)

ticks.because: The International Phonetic Alphabet (1888) had standardized the description of speech sounds. The International Postal Union (1874) modeled how systems could be defined by structural relationships. The Eiffel Tower (1889) and Lumière cinema (1895) demonstrated that modern artifacts were assembled from standardized parts. Saussure's posthumous Course distills the same insight for language — meaning is structural, words define each other through difference, and synchrony is more fundamental than history.

ticks.name: Dada movement
ticks.constraint: art as requiring skill, beauty, or coherent meaning
ticks.detail: Ancestor of surrealism, conceptual art, performance art.
ticks.because: The Futurism manifesto (1909) had argued that art should celebrate technological violence and rupture with tradition. Stravinsky's Rite of Spring (1913) demonstrated that modernism could provoke real cultural revolt. Dada is the post-WWI response — anti-art, anti-rationalism, anti-bourgeois, with collage, photomontage, and absurdist performance as its tools. Surrealism, conceptual art, and performance art all descend from Dada's sabotage.

ticks.name: Duchamp's Fountain (readymade)
ticks.constraint: art as requiring the artist's hand to create
ticks.detail: The artist's intention — not craft — as the defining act.

links.label: Monoskop: The Blind Man No. 2 (May 1917) — original Fountain publication

ticks.because: Saussure's synchronic linguistics and Course in General Linguistics (1916) had treated meaning as relational rather than essential. Stravinsky's Rite of Spring (1913) had demonstrated that radical art could provoke and survive scandal. Duchamp's signed urinal — submitted to a 1917 exhibition under the name R. Mutt — applies the same relational logic to art. The artist's intention rather than craft becomes the defining act, opening conceptual art's century-long career.

ticks.name: Women's suffrage (UK / US)
ticks.constraint: political citizenship as male by definition
ticks.detail: Half the population formally re-entered the political subject.

links.label: UK Parliament — Representation of the People Act 1918

ticks.because: Saussure's synchronic linguistics (1916) and Plessy v. Ferguson's separate-but-equal doctrine (1896) had each addressed the question of who counts in a system. Women's suffrage — the UK Representation of the People Act (1918) and the US Nineteenth Amendment (1920) — adds half the population to the political subject formally. The political consequences ripple for the rest of the century.

ticks.name: Radio broadcasting of music
ticks.constraint: music requiring physical attendance
ticks.detail: Mass taste, mass stars, and the possibility of a pop monoculture all begin here.

links.label: Penn State — KDKA: Broadcasting's Pioneer Station
World Radio History — It Started Hear KDKA (PDF)

ticks.because: Duchamp's Fountain (1917), De Stijl (1917), and the Bauhaus founding (1919) had each broken art's traditional link to physical objects and craft traditions. Radio broadcasting of music is the same dematerialization in sound — a single performance reaches millions of households simultaneously. Mass taste, mass stars, and the possibility of a pop monoculture all begin here.

ticks.name: Insulin (Banting/Best)
ticks.constraint: type 1 diabetes as a death sentence
ticks.detail: One of medicine's most dramatic reversals.

links.label: Banting & Best — The Internal Secretion of the Pancreas (1922)

ticks.because: The Flexner Report (1910) had professionalized medical education. The Spanish flu (1918) had taught the scale of public-health crises. Casimir Funk's vitamin concept (1912) demonstrated that biology could pin specific molecules to specific functions. Banting and Best's purification of insulin from canine pancreas extracts is the same molecular logic applied to diabetes — a single hormone, identified, isolatable, transferable. One of medicine's most dramatic reversals.

ticks.name: de Broglie wave-particle duality for matter
ticks.constraint: wave-particle duality as limited to light
ticks.detail: Everything is simultaneously wave and particle. Electron microscopy and quantum computing require matter waves.

links.label: American Institute of Physics — De Broglie's matter waves

ticks.because: Einstein's general relativity (1915-1916) had unified gravity with spacetime geometry. Eddington's eclipse confirmation (1919) made the theoretical victory public. The Stern-Gerlach experiment (1922) showed spatial quantization. De Broglie's hypothesis — that matter has wavelength λ = h/p — extends wave-particle duality from light to all matter. Electron microscopy and quantum mechanics's conceptual structure both depend on this insight.

ticks.name: Quantum mechanics (Heisenberg / Schrödinger)
ticks.constraint: quantum behavior as lacking a complete mathematical framework
ticks.detail: Foundation of modern physics: chemistry, solid-state physics, and all quantum technology.

links.label: David Lindley — Uncertainty: Einstein, Heisenberg, Bohr

ticks.because: De Broglie's matter-wave hypothesis (1924) and Bose-Einstein statistics (1924) had each pushed quantum reasoning to fundamental scales. Heisenberg's matrix mechanics (1925) and Schrödinger's wave equation (the same 1925-1926 cluster) provide the formal machinery. Quantum mechanics as a complete theory is in place by 1926; chemistry, solid-state physics, and every later quantum technology depend on it.

ticks.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
ticks.constraint: physical reality as precisely determinable in principle
ticks.detail: The universe is irreducibly probabilistic at the smallest scale.

links.label: NASA Technical Reports: Heisenberg 1927 paper translation (PDF)

ticks.because: Bose-Einstein statistics (1924), the formal quantum mechanics of 1925, and Schrödinger's wave equation (1926) established the formal apparatus. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is the philosophical-physical consequence — position and momentum cannot both be measured precisely; the universe is irreducibly probabilistic at the smallest scale. Determinism in physics is decisively challenged.

ticks.name: Heparin anticoagulant
ticks.constraint: blood clotting during surgery as unmanageable
ticks.detail: Made bypass machines, dialysis, and catheterization possible.

links.label: NCBI PMC — Discovery of heparin: history

ticks.because: Insulin's discovery and clinical deployment (1921) had demonstrated that purified biological molecules could revolutionize disease management. Muller's X-ray-induced mutations (1927) extended biology's molecular precision. Heparin's identification — a naturally occurring anticoagulant — provides the molecule that makes every later cardiovascular intervention possible. Bypass machines, dialysis, and catheterization all require heparin.

ticks.name: Penicillin (Fleming)
ticks.constraint: bacterial infection as often fatal
ticks.detail: Discovered 1928; deployed 1943 — a 15-year gap. The tick and its impact are often a generation apart.

links.label: Eric Lax — The Mold in Dr. Florey's Coat

ticks.because: Insulin's clinical deployment (1921) had proven that purified biological molecules could revolutionize disease management. Heparin's anticoagulant role (1928) and the tetanus toxoid vaccine (1924) demonstrated parallel biochemical maturation. Fleming's chance observation of Penicillium notatum killing staph cultures sits dormant for fifteen years until Florey and Chain industrialize production for WWII. The antibiotic era begins, with profound impact and increasingly visible costs.

ticks.name: EEG (electroencephalogram)
ticks.constraint: brain electrical activity as unobservable in living humans
ticks.detail: Also the first evidence that mental states have physical signatures.

links.label: Springer: Berger, Über das Elektrenkephalogramm des Menschen (1929)
Max Planck Institute: Berger 1929 EEG record

ticks.because: Heparin (1928) and penicillin's discovery (1928) had marked the late 1920s as a peak biomedical period. Hans Berger's electroencephalogram demonstrates that the brain produces electrical signals readable through the skull — and that those signals correlate with mental state. The first evidence that mental states have physical signatures; modern neuroscience and clinical neurology begin from this measurement.

ticks.name: Keynesian economics (after the crash)
ticks.constraint: markets as self-correcting without government intervention
ticks.detail: Deficit spending, automatic stabilizers, and the modern welfare state all trace to this tick.

links.label: Wikipedia: The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money
CEPR/VoxEU: Macroeconomic paradigm shifts and Keynes's General Theory

ticks.name: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
ticks.constraint: mathematics as completable and self-verifying
ticks.detail: Mathematics cannot bootstrap its own consistency. The most important result in logic since Aristotle.

links.label: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy — Kurt Gödel

ticks.because: Wittgenstein's Tractatus (1921) had argued that language could fully picture the world if its logic were exact enough. Heidegger's Being and Time (1927) had pulled philosophy back toward existential primacy of the lived world. Gödel's incompleteness theorems are the formal proof that Hilbert's program of complete consistent mathematics cannot succeed — every sufficiently powerful formal system contains true statements it cannot prove. Mathematics gains its first hard self-knowledge limit.

ticks.name: Neutron discovery (Chadwick)
ticks.constraint: the atomic nucleus as composed only of protons
ticks.detail: Immediately explained isotopes. Enabled nuclear reactions and radiocarbon dating.

links.label: Chadwick — Possible Existence of a Neutron (Nature 1932)

ticks.because: Dirac's equation (1928) had just predicted antimatter and unified quantum mechanics with special relativity, and Hubble's law (1929) had reframed cosmology around an expanding universe. Chadwick's bombardment of beryllium with alpha particles produced a neutral penetrating radiation — neutrons — that proton-only nuclear models could not explain, and immediately resolved the nuclear-mass arithmetic that had plagued physics for a decade.

ticks.name: Antimatter / positron (Anderson)
ticks.constraint: matter as having only one form
ticks.detail: PET scans are the medical application. Matter-antimatter asymmetry is physics' deepest unsolved problem.

links.label: Phys Rev: Anderson, The Positive Electron (1933)
Phys Rev: Anderson, Energies of Cosmic-Ray Particles (1932)

ticks.because: Hubble's expanding universe (1929) had reordered cosmology. Anderson's cloud-chamber detection of the positron — a particle with the electron's mass but opposite charge — confirms Dirac's prediction that quantum field theory required antimatter. PET scans become the medical application; matter-antimatter asymmetry remains physics' deepest cosmological puzzle.

ticks.name: Nylon (DuPont)
ticks.constraint: strong flexible fibers requiring biological production
ticks.detail: Materials could be engineered from scratch. Plastics, synthetic rubber, and polymer science all follow.

links.label: American Chemical Society: Wallace Carothers and modern polymer science (PDF)
PBS Science Odyssey: Nylon is invented (1935)

ticks.because: Pre-1935 strong fibers had been biological — silk, cotton, wool, linen — with the supply constraints of agriculture. Wallace Carothers's DuPont team (1935) synthesized polyamide-6,6 by polycondensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. Nylon stockings (1939) were the consumer launch; military parachutes and ropes were the wartime use. The first fully-synthetic high-strength fiber. Polyester, polyethylene, polypropylene, Kevlar all follow the same template — engineered polymers with engineered properties.

ticks.name: Turing's universal machine
ticks.constraint: computation as domain-specific
ticks.detail: Every computer ever built is a Turing machine.

links.label: Turing, A.M. — On Computable Numbers (1936) — original paper
Andrew Hodges — Alan Turing: The Enigma

ticks.because: Lovelace's first algorithm (1843) showed that mechanism could perform symbolic work. Hollerith's punch-card tabulator (1890) ran census data through hardware. The differential analyser (1931) put the idea into a working analog computer. Turing's universal machine — a thought-experiment device with a tape, a read-head, and a state — proved that any computation, no matter how specialized, could be performed by one general-purpose machine. Every computer ever built is a Turing machine.

ticks.name: Shannon's information theory
ticks.constraint: information as informal and context-dependent
ticks.detail: Data compression, error correction, internet protocols, and cryptography all build on Shannon's framework.

links.label: Shannon — A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948) — original paper
Jimmy Soni & Rob Goodman — A Mind at Play (Shannon biography)

ticks.name: First controlled nuclear chain reaction
ticks.constraint: nuclear energy as theoretical
ticks.detail: Enrico Fermi's team. The proof of concept for both nuclear weapons and nuclear power.
ticks.because: Hahn and Strassmann's discovery of fission (1939) — confirmed by Meitner and Frisch — proved that uranium could be split, releasing predictable energy per E=mc². Rabi's nuclear magnetic resonance (1938) proved that nuclear states could be measured precisely. Fermi's 1942 chain reaction is the engineering response: a self-sustaining controlled reaction is built once you can measure both the input (neutron capture) and the energy released. From here it is seven years to the bomb and twenty to civilian power.

ticks.name: Maslow's hierarchy of needs
ticks.constraint: human motivation as single-dimensional
ticks.detail: Product design, HR, and management theory were restructured around this pyramid.
ticks.because: Behaviorism (1913) had treated human motivation as response to drives — hunger, thirst, pain, pleasure. Maslow's 1943 paper 'A Theory of Human Motivation' proposed a hierarchy: physiological needs at the base, then safety, belonging, esteem, and self-actualization at the apex. Higher needs only emerge once lower ones are met. The pyramid is a postwar pop-culture infographic that Maslow himself never drew. Restructured product design, HR practice, and management theory around hierarchical motivation.

ticks.name: Blalock-Taussig shunt (pediatric heart surgery)
ticks.constraint: congenital heart defects as untreatable death sentences
ticks.detail: The first successful pediatric cardiac surgery — proof that the heart could be operated on in a living child.

links.label: Johns Hopkins Libraries: The Blalock-Taussig-Thomas Shunt exhibit
Johns Hopkins Medicine: Blalock-Taussig-Thomas Pediatric Heart Center history

ticks.because: Sulfonamides (1937) gave surgery its first reliable anti-bacterials. Blood banking (1940) made transfusion a reliable surgical input. The Rh factor (1940) eliminated previously inexplicable transfusion deaths. The Blalock-Taussig shunt is the first successful pediatric cardiac surgery — a small subclavian-to-pulmonary anastomosis that gives blue babies pink skin within minutes. Cardiac surgery as a discipline begins.

ticks.name: Bretton Woods Agreement
ticks.constraint: international currency exchange as bilateral and chaotic
ticks.detail: Created the institutional infrastructure — IMF, World Bank, GATT/WTO — that still governs global trade.

links.label: World Bank Archives: Bretton Woods and the Birth of the World Bank
IMF Site: The Bretton Woods Conference — Birth of a Monetary System
World Bank: Bretton Woods Monetary Conference, July 1-22, 1944

ticks.because: Nylon's invention by DuPont (1935) had demonstrated that designer materials could create entirely new commercial categories. Keynes's General Theory (1936) and Turing's universal machine (1936) had each given mid-1930s thinking radical new frameworks. The Bretton Woods Agreement of 1944 creates the postwar institutional infrastructure — IMF, World Bank, GATT/WTO — anchoring the postwar global economic order on dollar-gold convertibility.

ticks.name: Nuremberg Trials simultaneous interpretation
ticks.constraint: multilingual legal proceedings requiring sequential translation
ticks.detail: International diplomacy and the UN depend on this tick.

links.label: Robert H. Jackson Center — Nuremberg Trials
Holocaust Encyclopedia (USHMM) — International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg
AIIC — Origin of simultaneous interpretation at Nuremberg

ticks.because: Saussure's synchronic linguistics (1916) had treated language as a self-contained system; the Oxford English Dictionary (1928) had codified one such system at full scale. Brecht's epic theater (1928) and Citizen Kane (1941) had pushed the limits of what a single performance could carry across audiences. Nuremberg combines the threads at scale — four-language simultaneous interpretation, with translators speaking even as the speaker continues. The technical infrastructure of every UN session and EU summit since.

ticks.name: Atomic bomb
ticks.constraint: great-power war as a normal instrument of policy
ticks.detail: Nuclear deterrence may have prevented WWIII.

links.label: Richard Rhodes — The Making of the Atomic Bomb (Pulitzer Prize)
Atomic Heritage Foundation: Trinity test documents

ticks.because: Operation Overlord deception (1944) and D-Day amphibious doctrine (1944) had demonstrated WWII's industrial coordination at its peak. The jet engine (1944) showed that physics-engineered systems could leap technical generations in months. The atomic bomb's use at Hiroshima and Nagasaki is the same trajectory taken to species-altering scale — Manhattan Project physics deployed as a weapon, with deterrence replacing direct conflict between nuclear powers for the next eight decades.

ticks.name: United Nations / international law
ticks.constraint: international relations as purely transactional between sovereign states
ticks.detail: The tick was the idea: states have obligations beyond their borders.

links.label: United Nations — History of the UN

ticks.because: Wittgenstein's Tractatus (1921), Heidegger's Being and Time (1927), and the OED's completion (1928) bracket a moment when European thought was producing its most influential 20th-century philosophy and reference works — and Nazi Germany was preparing to test the very international order those works documented. The UN Charter (1945) gave the post-war world a framework for international law as more than transactional sovereign-state diplomacy, and enshrined human rights and collective security as binding obligations.

ticks.name: Indian independence / decolonization wave
ticks.constraint: European empire as permanent global order
ticks.detail: The political map of the world was redrawn in 30 years.

links.label: UK National Archives: Mountbatten radio broadcast (Jun 1947)

ticks.because: Gandhi's satyagraha (1919-1947) made British colonial rule politically unsustainable. WWII (1939-45) broke Britain's fiscal capacity to enforce it. Indian Independence (August 15, 1947) and Pakistan's simultaneous founding remade the political map of Asia. Within fifteen years, the European empires that had spanned the globe in 1939 were nearly gone. The post-colonial state became the dominant political form.

ticks.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
ticks.constraint: rights as granted by states to citizens
ticks.detail: Every human rights movement since invokes this document.

links.label: United Nations — Universal Declaration of Human Rights
Britannica — Universal Declaration of Human Rights

ticks.because: Nuremberg (1945-46) had judged crimes against humanity but not stated the rights they had violated. Eleanor Roosevelt's UN drafting committee (1947-48), drawing on the French Declaration (1789), the US Bill of Rights, and Latin American constitutional traditions, produced the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948). Thirty articles. Not a treaty, but a statement. Every subsequent human-rights convention — civil and political, economic and social, against torture, against discrimination — grew out of these thirty articles.

ticks.name: Magnetic tape recording
ticks.constraint: recording as a one-take, real-time capture
ticks.detail: The studio becomes an instrument.

links.label: Ampex — History of the Early Days of Ampex (PDF)

ticks.because: Citizen Kane (1941) had shown that cinematic editing could become its own narrative grammar. Abstract Expressionism (1947) demonstrated that the artistic process — gesture, drip, all-over composition — was as important as the result. Magnetic tape recording extends the editable-process logic into sound — the studio becomes an instrument, takes can be cut and rearranged, layers can be overdubbed. Modern record production begins.

ticks.name: Lithium for bipolar disorder
ticks.constraint: severe mood disorders as purely psychological and untreatable
ticks.detail: The first effective pharmacological treatment for a major psychiatric disorder. The era of psychopharmacology begins here.

links.label: NCBI/PMC: Cade, Lithium Salts in Treatment of Psychotic Excitement (1949)

ticks.because: The Blalock-Taussig shunt (1944), Kolff's dialysis machine (1943), and Avery's identification of DNA as genetic material (1944) demonstrated that mid-century medicine was acquiring molecular and engineering precision. Cade's lithium experiments on guinea pigs and then bipolar patients in 1949 demonstrate the first effective pharmacological treatment for a major psychiatric disorder. Psychiatric medicine becomes systematically pharmacological.

ticks.name: First nuclear electricity generation
ticks.constraint: electricity generation requiring combustion
ticks.detail: Nuclear power now generates ~10% of the world's electricity with near-zero carbon emissions.

links.label: OSTI: The Birth of Nuclear-Generated Electricity
Idaho National Laboratory: Experimental Breeder Reactor-I

ticks.because: Bretton Woods (1944) and the Marshall Plan (1947) had established the financial substrate for industrial-scale public infrastructure. Von Neumann architecture (1945) and ENIAC (1946) gave the engineering and computational tools. The first nuclear electricity generation (EBR-I, Idaho, 1951) is the demonstration that the same physics that built the bomb could light four light bulbs — the start of civilian nuclear power.

ticks.name: REM sleep discovery
ticks.constraint: sleep as a passive, undifferentiated state
ticks.detail: Sleep is an active, structured process. Memory consolidation and the neuroscience of consciousness are downstream.

links.label: NCBI PMC — Aserinsky and Kleitman 1953 REM discovery

ticks.because: Kolff's dialysis machine (1943), lithium for bipolar disorder (1949), and the first observation of antibiotic resistance in penicillin (1950) demonstrated that mid-century medicine was acquiring molecular and engineering precision. Aserinsky and Kleitman's REM sleep observation — rapid eye movements during specific sleep periods, correlated with vivid dreams — shows that sleep is an active structured process. Modern sleep science begins.

ticks.name: DNA double helix (Watson/Crick/Franklin)
ticks.constraint: heredity as a process without a physical substrate
ticks.detail: Biology became an engineering problem. Genomics, biotech, CRISPR all trace back here.

links.label: Watson & Crick — Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids (Nature 1953)
Brenda Maddox — Rosalind Franklin: The Dark Lady of DNA

ticks.because: Avery's identification of DNA as the genetic material (1944) and Hershey-Chase's confirmation (1952) had pinned heredity to the molecule. Antibiotic resistance (1950) had demonstrated rapid molecular evolution in bacteria. Watson, Crick, and Franklin's double helix in 1953 gives DNA its structure — and the structure immediately suggests the replication mechanism. Biology becomes an engineering problem; genomics, biotech, and CRISPR all trace to this paper.

ticks.name: First open-heart surgery (Gibbon)
ticks.constraint: the beating heart as unsurgeable
ticks.detail: The first time the heart could be stopped and restarted.

links.label: Jefferson DC: Dr. John Gibbon and the heart-lung machine (PDF)

ticks.because: Lithium for bipolar disorder (1949) had demonstrated mid-century medicine's pharmacological precision. Gibbon's heart-lung machine — twenty years in development — performs its first successful clinical use in 1953. The heart can be stopped and restarted; cardiac surgery becomes possible. Every later open-heart procedure depends on Gibbon's bypass.

ticks.name: Brown v. Board of Education
ticks.constraint: racial segregation as constitutionally permissible
ticks.detail: The legal foundation of American apartheid cracked.

links.label: National Archives (US) — Brown v. Board of Education
Britannica — Brown v. Board of Education

ticks.because: Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations (1953), the Nuremberg Principles establishing individual criminal responsibility (1950), and the European Convention on Human Rights (1950) bracket the post-WWII moment when both philosophy and international law were being reconstructed around individual rights. Brown v. Board of Education (1954) — overruling Plessy's separate-but-equal — extended the same individual-rights logic into US constitutional law, and triggered the civil rights movement that reordered American politics for the next two decades.

ticks.name: Polio vaccine (Salk / oral Sabin)
ticks.constraint: childhood paralysis epidemics as unstoppable
ticks.detail: Global polio cases dropped from 350,000 per year in 1988 to fewer than 30 today.

links.label: Sabin — Oral poliovirus vaccine: history (JAMA 1965, PubMed)
Eisenhower Library — Jonas Salk and the Polio Vaccine
Science History Institute — Salk and Sabin

ticks.because: Gibbon's first open-heart surgery (1953), Kolff's dialysis machine (1943), and the first successful kidney transplant (1954) demonstrated that mid-century medicine was rapidly conquering previously fatal conditions. Salk's killed-virus polio vaccine (1955) and later Sabin's oral attenuated version essentially eliminate paralytic polio in developed countries. Global polio cases drop from 350,000 per year in 1988 to fewer than thirty today.

ticks.name: Cognitive revolution (Miller, Chomsky)
ticks.constraint: mind as a black box to be described only by inputs and outputs
ticks.detail: Cognitive science as a discipline begins here.

links.label: ScienceDirect: Miller, The Cognitive Revolution: A Historical Perspective

ticks.because: Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations (1953) had reframed meaning as use. Hebb's synaptic plasticity rule (1949) gave neuroscience its first computational principle. Turing's machine-intelligence test (1950) had legitimized the computational study of mind. The 1956 cognitive revolution brings together Miller's seven-plus-or-minus-two, Chomsky's transformational grammar, and Newell-Simon's logical theorist — cognitive science as a discipline begins.

ticks.name: Neutrino detected (Cowan/Reines)
ticks.constraint: particles without charge as undetectable
ticks.detail: Pauli had predicted the neutrino in 1930; it took 26 years to detect it.
ticks.because: Holography (1947) had proven that wave physics could be engineered into useful devices. The solar cell (1954) and the maser (1953) showed that quantum predictions could be turned into commercial instruments. Cowan and Reines's neutrino detection extends the same trick to the most elusive particle — using a nuclear reactor as the neutrino source and a vat of cadmium-doped water as the detector. The neutrino joins the directly observed particle list.

ticks.name: Chomsky's generative grammar
ticks.constraint: language as a learned behavior (behaviorism)
ticks.detail: Language is generated by an innate universal grammar. Cognitive science and language acquisition were permanently transformed.

links.label: Culicover — The History of Syntax (Ohio State PDF)

ticks.because: Nuremberg's simultaneous interpretation (1945), the Weaver memo on machine translation (1949), and rock and roll's youth culture (1955) demonstrated that language was rapidly becoming a substrate for mass-cultural and computational engineering. Chomsky's Syntactic Structures formalizes the linguistic side — sentences generated by hierarchical upheaval rules from abstract deep structures. Cognitive science and language technology begin here.

ticks.name: Sputnik (first satellite)
ticks.constraint: outer space as beyond human reach
ticks.detail: Satellites now manage GPS, weather forecasting, communications, spy agencies, and financial markets.
ticks.because: ICBM development (1957), the Korean War's lessons in limited war (1950), Soviet Spetsnaz doctrine (1950), and the neutrino's detection (1956) frame the late-1950s moment when superpower competition was being projected into new domains. Sputnik 1 — 184 lbs, beeping at 20.005 MHz — orbited the Earth every 96 minutes and triggered the Space Race, NASA's founding, DARPA, and a wholesale reorganization of US science and education.

ticks.name: Cardiac pacemaker (implantable)
ticks.constraint: heart rhythm disorders as untreatable
ticks.detail: Millions of people with arrhythmias now live normal lives because of this.

links.label: NCBI PMC — History of the implantable cardiac pacemaker

ticks.because: The Blalock-Taussig shunt (1944), lithium for bipolar disorder (1949), and the Salk polio vaccine (1955) demonstrated mid-century medicine acquiring transformative interventions. The implantable cardiac pacemaker — Wilson Greatbatch's accidentally-correct circuit, miniaturized — is the same engineering applied to heart rhythm. Millions of people with arrhythmias live normal lives because of this device.

ticks.name: Perceptron (Rosenblatt)
ticks.constraint: machine learning as requiring explicit programming of every rule
ticks.detail: The architecture — weighted inputs, threshold activation, error-driven learning — is exactly what modern neural networks use.

links.label: IEEE Xplore — The Perceptron (Ideas That Created the Future)

ticks.because: FORTRAN (1957) and the Fortran compiler had each given the era its first high-level programming language. Rosenblatt's Perceptron — weighted inputs, threshold activation, error-driven learning — is the first working neural network. The architecture is theoretically limited (Minsky-Papert 1969) but conceptually correct; sixty years later, deep neural networks are direct descendants.

ticks.name: Stokoe proves ASL is a full language
ticks.constraint: sign languages as simplified gesture, not real language
ticks.detail: Sign languages are independent, fully expressive linguistic systems.

links.label: Oxford JDSDE: Sign Language Structure reprint

ticks.because: Chomsky's transformational grammar (1957) and his universal grammar hypothesis (1957) had argued that language was a deep cognitive system, not a culturally arbitrary surface phenomenon. Stokoe's notation system applied to American Sign Language proves that ASL has the same structural properties as spoken languages — phonology, morphology, syntax. Sign languages are recognized as full languages, not pantomime.

ticks.name: Seafloor spreading (Hess)
ticks.constraint: the ocean floor as ancient and geologically static
ticks.detail: New ocean crust continuously created at mid-ocean ridges — the mechanism for continental drift.

links.label: USGS — Developing the Theory: Seafloor Spreading
Princeton — Harry Hess and seafloor spreading

ticks.because: Cowan-Reines neutrino detection (1956) and Feynman's 'Plenty of Room' speech (1959) demonstrated that careful engineering could reveal phenomena previously thought inaccessible. The integrated circuit (1958) showed that complex systems could be built from miniaturized parts. Hess's seafloor spreading hypothesis — new ocean crust continuously created at mid-ocean ridges — is the same pattern in geology. Continental drift gets its mechanism, and plate tectonics emerges as a unified theory.

ticks.name: Laser (Maiman)
ticks.constraint: coherent, concentrated light as physically impossible
ticks.detail: Barcode scanners, optical fiber communications, surgery, DVD players, and laser cutting all require coherent light.
ticks.because: Feynman's 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom' (1959) had argued that engineering at small scales would unlock entire new physical regimes. Maiman's ruby laser is the first major instance — coherent, monochromatic, directional light produced from a small synthetic crystal. Barcode scanners, fiber-optic communication, surgery, and DVD playback all need this device.

ticks.name: The Pill (oral contraceptive)
ticks.constraint: female reproductive autonomy requiring male cooperation
ticks.detail: Removed the biological constraint that had structured women's lives since the beginning of human history.

links.label: Wikipedia: Combined oral contraceptive pill — history
Jonathan Eig — The Birth of the Pill

ticks.because: Chlorpromazine (1952), the cardiac pacemaker (1958), and Leakey's Olduvai Gorge work (1959) had each marked late-1950s medicine as a peak interventional period. Pincus, Rock, and Chang's combined oral contraceptive — approved 1960 — removes the biological constraint that had structured women's lives for the entire human past. Demographic, social, and economic structures reorder over the following two generations.

ticks.name: Integrated circuit (Kilby/Noyce)
ticks.constraint: physical scale of computation
ticks.detail: Moore's Law follows. The chip is the compounding engine of the modern world.
ticks.because: Hess's seafloor spreading (1960), Maiman's laser (1960), and McCarthy's time-sharing computing (1960) demonstrated rapid mid-century technical maturation. Kilby and Noyce's parallel inventions of the integrated circuit — multiple components fabricated together on a single semiconductor substrate — are the platform that allows Moore's Law to play out. The chip becomes the compounding engine of every later computing era.

ticks.name: Human spaceflight (Gagarin)
ticks.constraint: humans as Earth-bound
ticks.detail: Earthrise (1968) credited with launching the environmental movement.

links.label: NASA — Yuri Gagarin: First Human in Space
History.com — Gagarin first man in space

ticks.because: Counterinsurgency doctrine (1960), the U-2 incident's reordering of strategic intelligence (1960), and Hess's seafloor spreading (1960) demonstrated that 1960 was a peak strategic-technological moment. Gagarin's April 1961 orbit — the first human in space — shocks the United States into the Apollo commitment. Earthrise photographs from 1968 are credited with launching the environmental movement; space-borne perspective on Earth becomes a recurring cultural touchstone.

ticks.name: Silent Spring (Rachel Carson)
ticks.constraint: nature as an infinite, passive resource for human use
ticks.detail: The modern environmental movement begins here.

links.label: Bellarmine/Merton: Silent Spring full text PDF

ticks.because: Sartre's Being and Nothingness (1943), operations research (1945), and Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations (1953) demonstrated mid-century intellectual willingness to challenge received frames at the deepest level. Carson's Silent Spring applies the same critical posture to the chemical industry's pesticide use — DDT's downstream ecological costs documented systematically. The modern environmental movement begins here.

ticks.name: Kidney transplant (long-term success)
ticks.constraint: end-stage kidney disease as a death sentence
ticks.detail: Immunosuppression made organ transplantation broadly applicable.

links.label: NCBI PMC — History of kidney transplantation

ticks.because: By 1954, antibiotics, blood typing, and dialysis had made transplant surgery imaginable; the Murray-Merrill team's identical-twin kidney transplant in Boston is the first long-term success. Removing one organ from one body and connecting it to another, with the recipient surviving for decades, is the proof that organs are interchangeable parts. Modern transplant medicine begins.

ticks.name: The Feminine Mystique (Betty Friedan)
ticks.constraint: women's dissatisfaction as personal failure rather than structural
ticks.detail: The second-wave feminist movement begins here.

links.label: Jewish Women's Archive — Publication of Feminine Mystique

ticks.because: Chomsky's transformational grammar (1957) had reframed mind as governed by deep structures invisible from the surface. Carson's Silent Spring (1962) and Kuhn's Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962) had proven that received frameworks could be challenged with rigor. The Dartmouth AI workshops (1956) had demonstrated that institutions can name a discipline into existence. Friedan applies the same maneuver to women's experience — the dissatisfaction is structural, not personal, and naming it builds a movement.

ticks.name: Quark model (Gell-Mann / Zweig)
ticks.constraint: protons and neutrons as fundamental particles
ticks.detail: The Standard Model's quark sector and quantum chromodynamics follow directly.

links.label: OSTI.GOV: Gell-Mann, A Schematic Model of Baryons and Mesons (1964)

ticks.because: The Josephson effect (1962) showed that quantum behavior crossed solid-state interfaces predictably, and the laser (1960) plus the Cosmic Microwave Background discovery (1965) bracket a period when particle physics was producing more states than the existing nucleon model could absorb. Gell-Mann and Zweig independently proposed quarks — three-flavor substructure — and turned a confusing zoo of mesons and baryons into a clean group-theoretic picture.

ticks.name: Higgs mechanism (theoretical)
ticks.constraint: mass as a fundamental unexplained property
ticks.detail: 48 years from theory to experimental proof.

links.label: Nobel Prize — François Englert and Peter W. Higgs 2013

ticks.because: The Josephson effect (1962) and the laser (1960) demonstrated that gauge symmetries and coherent quantum states governed condensed-matter behavior, and the same year as the quark model (1964) saw the question of mass left unresolved by the Standard Model so far. Higgs, Englert, Brout, and Kibble proposed spontaneous symmetry breaking via a scalar field — a mechanism that would wait 48 years for the LHC to confirm it.

ticks.name: Plate tectonics unified theory
ticks.constraint: geology as a collection of unrelated regional observations
ticks.detail: Geology became predictive science. Every earthquake prediction uses plate tectonics.

links.label: Naomi Oreskes — The Rejection of Continental Drift

ticks.because: Bell's theorem (1964) proved that quantum reality required nonlocal correlations — physics was committing to deeply unintuitive predictions. Plate tectonics is the geological equivalent — Earth's crust is broken into rigid plates floating on a plastic mantle, drifting at centimeters per year, generating earthquakes and volcanoes at their boundaries. Geology becomes a predictive science.

ticks.name: Nouvelle Vague / jump cut (Godard)
ticks.constraint: film editing requiring continuous spatial-temporal logic
ticks.detail: Cinema became self-aware.

links.label: Intellect: Jump Cuts in Godard's Breathless
P.O.V.: Five Explanations for Jump Cuts in Godard's Breathless

ticks.because: Chomsky's transformational grammar (1957) and his universal grammar hypothesis (1957) demonstrated that language could be analyzed at deep structural levels. Rock and roll (1955) made cultural form-breaking commercial. Godard's jump cut in Breathless (1960) applies the same form-breaking logic to cinema — eliminating continuity editing, making time discontinuous, the camera self-aware. Modern art-cinema syntax is established.

ticks.name: First heart transplant (Barnard)
ticks.constraint: organ failure as irreversible
ticks.detail: Ethical frameworks around death and donation were invented to accommodate this.

links.label: NCBI PMC — Christiaan Barnard and the first human heart transplant
Heart of Cape Town Museum (Groote Schuur) — first heart transplant

ticks.because: The first kidney transplant (1954) and Starzl's liver transplant (1963) had proven complex organ surgery could succeed. The full genetic code's deciphering (1966) marked biology's molecular maturity. Barnard's heart transplant in Cape Town extends transplantation to the most symbolically loaded organ — and forces ethical frameworks around brain death, donation, and the medical definition of life to be redrafted.

ticks.name: Apollo 11 / moon landing
ticks.constraint: another celestial body as permanently unreachable
ticks.detail: A demonstration that sufficiently motivated states can do the apparently impossible.

links.label: NASA — 50 Years Ago: Apollo Astronauts Land

ticks.because: The Six-Day War's preemptive strike doctrine (1967) and the Tet Offensive's information warfare (1968) demonstrated that the late 1960s were a peak strategic-technological period. Apollo 11's July 1969 landing — Armstrong and Aldrin walking on the moon — demonstrates that sufficiently motivated states can do the apparently impossible. Cold War politics, civilian space exploration, and the techno-optimism of the era all crystallize around this event.

ticks.name: ARPANET / packet switching
ticks.constraint: network resilience requiring central routing
ticks.detail: Make the pipes dumb and the edges smart.
ticks.because: Engelbart's Mother of All Demos (1968) had shown that computers could become collaborative tools, with windows, hypertext, and the mouse all visible at once. Dijkstra's structured programming (1968) gave software the discipline to scale. ARPANET's packet-switching design (1969) closes the architectural picture — make the pipes dumb, make the edges smart, route around failure. The internet's founding principle is set.

ticks.name: Unix operating system
ticks.constraint: operating systems as hardware-specific and non-portable
ticks.detail: Linux, macOS, Android all descend from Unix.

links.label: Ritchie & Thompson — The UNIX Time-Sharing System (CACM 1974)
Brian Kernighan — UNIX: A History and a Memoir

ticks.because: Dijkstra's structured programming (1968) had argued that software could be made comprehensible by replacing GOTO chains with disciplined control flow. ARPANET's packet switching (1969) had proven that heterogeneous machines could share resources over a dumb network. Unix is the operating-system embodiment of both insights — a small kernel, composable utilities communicating through pipes, network-aware from early on. Linux, macOS, and Android all descend from this design.

ticks.name: Stonewall / LGBTQ+ rights movement
ticks.constraint: homosexuality as criminal and shameful
ticks.detail: From criminality to civil rights in one generation.

links.label: AP News — Stonewall: How a raid and rebellion became a rights movement
NPS — Stonewall National Monument: History & Culture

ticks.because: Derrida's deconstruction (1967), Miranda rights (1966), and Loving v. Virginia legalizing interracial marriage (1967) demonstrated that late-1960s American law and culture were rapidly liberalizing. Stonewall's June 1969 patron resistance to the police raid — and the subsequent organizing — launches the LGBTQ rights movement. From criminality to civil rights in one generation; same-sex marriage federally protected in the United States by 2015.

ticks.name: Email
ticks.constraint: asynchronous communication requiring physical proximity
ticks.detail: Coordination across time zones became effortless.

links.label: Multicians: The History of Electronic Mail (Tom Van Vleck)
The Verge: Ray Tomlinson interview, inventor of email

ticks.because: ARPANET's first message (1969) and the email precursor (1969) had established the network's existence. Synthetic organic chemistry's total synthesis (1970) demonstrated the era's broader engineering precision. Tomlinson's 1971 implementation of email between hosts — using @ to separate user from machine — formalizes asynchronous digital communication. Coordination across time zones becomes effortless; office work reorganizes around the inbox.

ticks.name: Microprocessor (Intel 4004)
ticks.constraint: computing requiring a room-sized machine
ticks.detail: The tick that moved computing from institution to individual.
ticks.because: Email (1971) had begun the move from terminals to networks; Intel's 1103 DRAM (1970) had killed magnetic core memory. The 4004 is the integration step — putting an entire CPU on a single chip. Computing's center of gravity moves from institutions to individuals over the next decade.

ticks.name: End of gold standard (Nixon)
ticks.constraint: money supply limited by physical gold reserves
ticks.detail: Money became pure fiat. Enabled the massive credit expansion of the late 20th century.

links.label: US State Dept Office of the Historian: Nixon and the End of Bretton Woods
Federal Reserve History: Nixon Ends Convertibility of US Dollars to Gold

ticks.because: The Modigliani-Miller theorem (1958), Akerlof's market for lemons (1970), and the ISO standardization of intermodal container sizes (1968) demonstrated that postwar finance and trade were institutionalizing. Nixon's August 1971 closing of the gold window ends the Bretton Woods system — money becomes pure fiat. The massive credit expansion and floating-currency volatility of the next half-century are direct consequences.

ticks.name: Recombinant DNA (Boyer/Cohen)
ticks.constraint: genetic information as readable but not editable
ticks.detail: The genetic code became programmable. Biotechnology as an industry starts here.

links.label: Cohen et al. — Construction of Biologically Functional Bacterial Plasmids (PNAS 1973)
National Human Genome Research Institute: Recombinant DNA history

ticks.because: Earth Day (1970), Favaloro's coronary artery bypass (1967), and the CT scanner's clinical introduction (1971) demonstrated that early-1970s medicine and biology were rapidly advancing. Boyer and Cohen's recombinant DNA work — using restriction enzymes to cut and ligate DNA from different organisms — turns the genetic code into a programmable object. Biotechnology as an industry begins; insulin, growth hormone, and modern pharmaceutical biology all stand on recombinant DNA.

ticks.name: MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
ticks.constraint: brain structure visible only post-mortem
ticks.detail: Brain tumors, strokes, MS plaques all became visible without surgery. Neuroscience became an imaging science.
ticks.because: The CT scanner's clinical introduction (1971) and the cochlear implant's first single-channel version (1972) demonstrated that early-1970s medical imaging and intervention were rapidly maturing. Lauterbur's MRI — applying NMR to medical imaging via spatial encoding — gives medicine its second three-dimensional non-invasive imaging modality. Brain tumors, strokes, and MS plaques become visible without surgery; modern diagnostic medicine acquires its workhorse instrument.

ticks.name: Black-Scholes options pricing model
ticks.constraint: options pricing as intuitive and inconsistent
ticks.detail: Made options trading tractable. Within 30 years, global derivatives exceeded $1 quadrillion in notional value.

links.label: Black & Scholes — The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities (JPE 1973)

ticks.because: The OPEC oil shock (1973) demonstrated that market-set prices were now the dominant reality, and the C programming language (1972) gave finance the computational substrate to do continuous calculation. Black, Scholes, and Merton's options-pricing formula gave traders an analytical model for pricing financial derivatives — and its publication coincided with the opening of the Chicago Board Options Exchange, triggering the financial-derivatives explosion.

ticks.name: Prospect theory (Kahneman/Tversky)
ticks.constraint: human decision-making as rational utility maximization
ticks.detail: Behavioral economics, nudge theory, every insurance product and health intervention.

links.label: Daniel Kahneman — Thinking, Fast and Slow

ticks.because: The Stanford Prison Experiment (1971) and Tversky-Kahneman's heuristics-and-biases work (1972) showed that human decision-making was systematically irrational in identifiable ways, and Csikszentmihalyi's flow research (1975) extended the empirical psychology of attention. Prospect theory (1979) replaced expected utility theory with an empirical decision model — losses loom larger than equivalent gains, decisions are made relative to a reference point — and won Kahneman the 2002 Nobel.

ticks.name: VisiCalc (spreadsheet)
ticks.constraint: recalculation as manual work
ticks.detail: The first killer app. Defined what personal computing was for.
ticks.because: Pre-VisiCalc spreadsheets had been paper grids that took hours to recalculate when an input changed. Dan Bricklin and Bob Frankston's VisiCalc (1979, on the Apple II) recalculated automatically — change one cell, the whole sheet updated. Apple II sales doubled. The first 'killer app' that made personal computing economically rational for businesses. Lotus 1-2-3 (IBM PC, 1983) and Excel (Mac, 1985) inherited the model; spreadsheets remain the most-used computing application after web browsing.

ticks.name: Public-key cryptography (Diffie-Hellman)
ticks.constraint: secure communication requiring prior exchange of secret keys
ticks.detail: HTTPS, SSH, PGP, and all secure internet communication depend on this. The entire digital economy runs on this tick.

links.label: Diffie & Hellman — New Directions in Cryptography (1976) — original paper
Steven Levy — Crypto: How the Code Rebels Beat the Government

ticks.because: The Altair 8800 (1975) and SQL (1974) demonstrated that personal computing and database access were rapidly maturing. Diffie and Hellman's public-key cryptography — sender encrypts with recipient's public key, only recipient's private key decrypts — solves the key-distribution problem that has limited cryptography for centuries. HTTPS, SSH, PGP, and all secure internet communication depend on this insight.

ticks.name: First IVF baby (Louise Brown)
ticks.constraint: conception requiring intercourse
ticks.detail: Fertility medicine, egg freezing, surrogacy, and the legal frameworks around reproductive technology all begin here.

links.label: ScienceDirect — First IVF baby: how it happened
BBC — 1978: First test tube baby born

ticks.because: Recombinant DNA (1973) had made the genetic code programmable, and Sanger sequencing (1977) plus PET (1974) gave medicine the molecular and imaging tools to act inside the body at unprecedented resolution. Steptoe and Edwards's IVF — fertilizing an egg outside the body and reimplanting it — extended the same toolkit to reproduction, and made fertility, surrogacy, and reproductive law a new domain.

ticks.name: Walkman (Sony)
ticks.constraint: music listening as stationary and shared
ticks.detail: The atomization of media consumption begins here.

links.label: NYT Archive: Sony Walkman 1979 (Humming Off Key for Two Decades)
Sony Corporate History: Walkman TPS-L2 milestones

ticks.because: Punk rock's DIY ethos (1976) and punk graphic design (1978) had recently legitimized personal cultural production at small scale. The Walkman applies the same individuation to consumption — every listener now carries their own playback, decoupled from speakers, family, or place. Media's atomization into individual experiences begins here.

ticks.name: Volcker's monetarist shock
ticks.constraint: high inflation as politically impossible to cure
ticks.detail: Established central bank independence as a core principle of monetary policy globally.

links.label: Federal Reserve History: Volcker's Anti-Inflation Measures
Federal Reserve: The Reform of October 1979 (PDF)
Minneapolis Fed: Reflections on Monetary Policy 25 Years After Oct 1979

ticks.because: Index funds (1975) demonstrated that disciplined rule-following could outperform discretionary management, and the 401(k) provision (1978) shifted retirement risk to households that were now exposed to inflation directly. Volcker's 20% Fed funds rate broke that political constraint — accepting recession to break inflation — and established central bank independence as a global norm.

ticks.name: Smallpox declared eradicated
ticks.constraint: the assumption that infectious diseases are permanent features of human life
ticks.detail: The first and only human disease deliberately eliminated. The template for polio and measles eradication.
ticks.because: The CT scanner (1971), IVF (1978), and balloon angioplasty (1977) signaled a decade in which disease processes that had felt permanent were being reduced to procedure-able problems. Smallpox eradication was the largest expression of that mood — coordinated global vaccination, ring containment, last natural case in Somalia 1977 — and the template applied since to polio and measles.

ticks.name: IBM PC + open architecture
ticks.constraint: hardware and software as bundled proprietary systems
ticks.detail: The commoditization of hardware shifted value to software.

links.label: Intel — The 8086 and the IBM PC

ticks.because: Unix (1969) had defined the open system architecture for software. Usenet (1979) had created the first online communities. VisiCalc (1979) had shown the personal computer's productivity case. The IBM PC's open architecture combines all three — third-party hardware via standard slots, third-party software via published APIs, and a clone-able BIOS. The PC ecosystem and the modern hardware-software market structure are set.

ticks.name: Currency swap (IBM/World Bank) — first modern derivative
ticks.constraint: cross-border currency exposure
ticks.detail: The 1981 IBM-World Bank deal pioneered the modern swap market via currency exchange, not interest rates.

links.label: ISDA: A First for Derivatives Markets
IBSCDC Case Study: IBM-World Bank Currency Swap

ticks.because: Volcker's monetarist shock (1979), recombinant insulin's biotech industry birth (1978), and VisiCalc's business-computer revolution (1979) had each marked the late 1970s as a structural reorganization.
